chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from al-Husayn, from al-Nadr and Fadalah, from Abd Allah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about the obligatory prayer on a ship, when he finds the land and can disembark, but he fears wild beasts and thieves, and there are people with him whose opinion does not unite on disembarking and they do not obey him. And whether he places his face (in prostration) when he prays, or signals with a nod, or prays sitting or standing? He said: 'If he is able to pray standing, that is better, and if he is not able, he prays sitting.'
And he said: 'There is no harm on him if he does not disembark, for a man asked my father about a similar issue, and he said: 'Do you prefer to miss the prayer of Noah?''

key_terms.صَلَاةُ نُوحٍ: Prayer of Noah (referencing the long duration of Noah's prayer)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for praying on a ship if you can get off but choose to stay due to fear or group disagreement?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the fiqh of prayer on vessels when disembarkation is possible but impractical due to fear or group discord, establishing a hierarchy of preference between standing and sitting. The Imam’s reference to his father, Imam al-Sadiq, and the rhetorical question 'Do you prefer [staying] over the prayer of Noah?' underscores the theological weight of maintaining ritual continuity even in precarious conditions, linking the believer's experience to the prophetic tradition of endurance during the Flood.
